expectations.text: Includes the CSV-to-HTTPS purpose, Python 3.12 and PostgreSQL 16 requirements, all three configuration/installation/use steps, preserving code strings.
expectations.evidence: “accepts CSV files and delivers their rows to a configured HTTPS endpoint”; “Python 3.12 and a PostgreSQL 16 service”; exact `pip install harbor-queue`, `DATABASE_URL`, `DESTINATION_URL` and `harbor-queue ingest orders.csv` appear.

expectations.text: Preserves at-least-once semantics, supplied delivery_id deduplication requirement, and does not imply exactly-once delivery.
expectations.evidence: “Delivery is at least once: a row may arrive more than once” and “must use the supplied `delivery_id` to deduplicate rows.”

expectations.text: Preserves 25 MB limit and no partial import on rejected files; accurately describes supplied Authorization header if authentication is mentioned.
expectations.evidence: “Files over 25 MB are rejected without importing any rows”; “Configure the `Authorization` header with the credential value your endpoint requires.”

expectations.text: Does not narrate the discarded macro, SQLite replacement/debug session, Redis branch, internal nickname, or review/editorial notes.
expectations.evidence: The text proceeds from “Quick start” through current “Delivery” and file limits; no discarded prototypes, internal nickname or editorial notes appear.

expectations.text: Does not present unshipped OAuth, S3 import, or dashboard as capabilities, or claim no external service is needed; at most 230 words.
expectations.evidence: “a PostgreSQL 16 service” preserves the external prerequisite; no OAuth/S3/dashboard capabilities appear. 107 whitespace-delimited words.

review_method: Independent single blind agent review; not human feedback
